usage: The everyday Iraqi hello, warm and fine for anyone, man or woman, friend or stranger. Iraqis rarely stop at one word: a hello is usually followed straight away by "shlonak?" and a round of blessings.

variants.label: formal / traditional
variants.note: The standard greeting when entering a shop, an office or a room full of people; always answered with "w-3alaikum is-salaam".

variants.label: extra warm
variants.note: Adds warmth when greeting one man; to a woman say "hala beech", to a group "hala beekum".

variants.label: casual
variants.note: Borrowed from English and very common among young people in Baghdad.
